body:
Closes # 680.

Every leg of this gate measures the fork against `refs/remotes/upstream/main`, and nothing established what that ref was worth. Straight after `just sync` it is current, because sync fetches. On its own, "HEAD contains upstream/main" was close to a tautology: an old commit is an ancestor of nearly anything, so a replay onto a stale upstream passed clean while the gate reported it had landed on upstream.

A fetch would be worse than the disease, and that reasoning is now in the file so nobody adds one later. Fetching origin moves the pre-rebase tip four checks compare against; fetching upstream moves the yardstick. `git ls-remote` asks without writing a ref, and an unreachable remote reports SKIP rather than passing quietly.

The new leg answers in commit counts and in upstream's own commit dates: what the replay landed on, how far the ref has moved since, and whether the ref is still the remote tip. It fails only when the ref differs from the remote and its tip is a week or more old.

Local clocks were tried first and are the wrong instrument, which is worth recording because they look right. Review took the first version apart: a fetch bringing nothing new writes no reflog entry, so a correct sync across a quiet weekend upstream read as stale (8 such gaps in the last 90 days), while any later fetch made a months-old replay read as current. It also computed the replay base and never compared it to the remote, so it printed `fresh` in exactly the state it existed to catch.

Two live bugs in # 669 turned up along the way, both the gate reporting what it had not established. They are here rather than in their own PRs because they are the same defect and the same lines.

The ancestor check failed on correct replays: any fetch after a sync moves the ref past what the replay targeted, and it was failing in this worktree for that reason. It also took the recipe down through `set -e`, printing no verdict at all, when two histories share no ancestor.

The build ladder never ran on Windows. The `just` path was unquoted, so bash ate the backslashes and the first leg died as `command not found`, reported as `build ladder: just build-dll failed`. The `break` meant the rest never ran. This is the leg the gate exists for.

Verified on a synthetic upstream and fork across eight states: on the tip, upstream advanced and fetched, upstream ahead and unfetched with a fresh tip, the same with a 30 day old tip, remote config removed with the tracking ref left behind, remote unreachable, no common history, and `timeout` absent from PATH. Exits 0 except the stale ref and the unrelated histories, which exit 1.
title: build: stop sync-verify trusting a ref it never checked
